pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.5 Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing (2 Sessions) • Punctuation mark
Topic 3.7: Guided Writing: Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you make a story more interesting in writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary
2. write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary

What this means
In this part you learn to construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words

What this means
In this part you learn to write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing: Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing: Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary.
3. Practise this skill: write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing: Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Guided Writing: Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you make a story more interesting in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing: Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary.
5. Be able to: write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
